name: LM74700QDBVRQ1
title: LM74700-Q1 low-IQ ideal diode controller for reverse battery protection
summary: An automotive ideal diode controller that drives an external N-channel MOSFET in series with a supply, holding its forward drop at 20 mV and turning it off within 0.75 µs when current reverses. It runs from 3.2 V to 65 V (3.9 V to start), withstands -65 V on its input, and has an internal charge pump for the gate. It draws 80 µA in operation and 1 µA with EN low. It comes in a 6-pin SOT-23 (DBV) and an 8-pin SOT-23-THIN (DDF); LM74700QDBVRQ1 is the DBV part on a 3000-piece reel.
key_figures: 3.2 V to 65 V, 3.9 V start-up; operating input voltage V(ANODE) 4 V to 60 V

notes: All are RoHS compliant production parts. The DBV and DDF packages differ in pin count and order and in thermal resistance; both are 2.90 mm × 1.60 mm nominal body.
An Enhanced Product version, LM74700-EP, exists for defense, aerospace and medical use.

circuits.title: Reverse battery protection with on/off control
circuits.description: An external N-channel MOSFET sits in series with the battery feed to a voltage regulator, its source on the battery side and its drain on the output. The controller senses the battery side on ANODE and the output on CATHODE and drives the MOSFET gate from GATE; a capacitor from VCAP to ANODE stores the charge pump energy. A bidirectional TVS and a capacitor sit across the input, a polarised capacitor across the output, and EN is brought out as an on/off control.

circuits.title: 12 V battery protection with one bidirectional TVS
circuits.description: The 12 V design example: a battery feeds a voltage regulator through Q1, which the LM74700-Q1 runs as an ideal diode. EN is tied to ANODE, so the controller is on whenever the battery is. An SMBJ33CA bidirectional TVS clamps both positive and negative surges at the input, 22 nF decouples the input, 0.1 µF from VCAP to ANODE holds the charge pump charge and 47 µF at the output holds the rail up through input disturbances.

parts.note: 60 V VDS(MAX), ±20 V VGS(MAX), RDS(ON) 6.5 mΩ typ and 8.5 mΩ max at VGS = 4.5 V, Vth 2 V max

notes: The design example targets a 12 V battery with 3.2 V cold crank and 35 V load dump, 3 A nominal and 5 A maximum load, and ISO 7637-2 and ISO 16750-2 compliance.

circuits.title: 24 V battery protection with two unidirectional TVS
circuits.description: The 24 V version of the same circuit. The input clamp is two unidirectional TVS diodes joined anode to anode: an SMBJ58A from the battery line and an SMBJ26A to ground. Input, charge pump and output capacitors are 22 nF, 0.1 µF and 47 µF, and EN is tied to ANODE. A 75 V MOSFET is named for this pairing of TVS diodes.

circuits.title: Two-supply OR-ing
circuits.description: Two supplies, VIN1 and VIN2, share one load. Each feeds the common output through its own MOSFET and LM74700-Q1, with EN tied to ANODE, a bidirectional TVS and an input capacitor on its supply, and a charge pump capacitor from VCAP to ANODE. Both drains and both CATHODE pins meet at VOUT, which carries the output capacitor and the load. The controller on whichever supply is lower sees reverse voltage and turns its MOSFET off, so a failed supply cannot pull the output down or back-feed the other.

operation.text: The controller and an external N-channel MOSFET together act as a diode with a very small drop. It watches the voltage between ANODE (MOSFET source) and CATHODE (MOSFET drain) and sets the gate so that the forward drop sits at 20 mV. If the drop falls below -11 mV the gate is shorted to ANODE at once and the body diode blocks the reverse current. A built-in charge pump lifts the gate up to about 15 V above ANODE. It replaces a Schottky diode or P-channel MOSFET for reverse polarity protection and can be used for OR-ing supplies.

ANODE powers the chip, which draws about 80 µA enabled and 1 µA disabled. Above the POR rising threshold it runs in shutdown or conduction according to EN. ANODE to GND may swing from -65 V to 65 V, so negative transients are survived. Operation runs down to 3.2 V once started; start-up needs 3.9 V.

A capacitor from VCAP to ANODE stores the gate drive energy. The pump runs only with EN above V(EN_IH) and charges at 300 µA typical. The gate driver is held off until VCAP - ANODE passes its undervoltage release, 6.6 V typical, with about 900 mV of hysteresis. The pump then cycles: off when VCAP - ANODE reaches 13 V, back on below 12.1 V, which lowers the average quiescent current. When off it sinks 5 µA typical.

GATE is held at ANODE, MOSFET off, until all three hold: EN above its high threshold, VCAP - ANODE above the undervoltage release, and ANODE above the POR rising threshold. After that the drive mode follows the ANODE - CATHODE voltage.
For an ANODE - CATHODE drop between -11 mV and 50 mV the gate voltage is trimmed to hold the drop at 20 mV. At light load the MOSFET is eased off gently, and no DC reverse current flows.

Once load current pushes the drop past about 50 mV, GATE is connected to VCAP, so the gate-source voltage equals the VCAP - ANODE voltage and the MOSFET reaches its lowest on-resistance for large currents.

When current reverses and the drop goes below about -11 mV, GATE is connected to ANODE, turning the MOSFET off; its body diode then blocks drain-to-source current. The response is under 0.75 µs, with a 2.3 A peak gate sink, suiting systems that need output hold-up through ISO 7637 pulse tests, input micro-shorts and power failures.

EN above the rising threshold runs the charge pump and gate driver; below the low threshold both stop and the part draws about 1 µA from ANODE. EN withstands ±65 V and may be wired straight to ANODE. Left open, an internal 3 µA sink holds it low and the part is off. In shutdown, forward current still reaches the load through the MOSFET body diode.

Its continuous drain current rating must exceed the maximum load current, its VDS rating must cover the largest voltage difference including faults (60 V parts are suggested, since anode to cathode is limited to 65 V), and its body diode must carry the inrush current that charges the output capacitance at start-up. The gate is driven to at most 13 V, so pick a MOSFET with a VGS rating of at least 15 V, or clamp VGS with a zener. Too low an RDS(ON) hurts reverse current detection: choose it so the drop at nominal current lands near 20 mV and no higher than 50 mV. Run the MOSFET near 4.5 V of gate drive at light load, well above threshold; a threshold of 2 V to 2.5 V maximum is preferred, and lower thresholds also turn on faster. For the 12 V example the targets were 60 V VDS, ±20 V VGS, 6.67 mΩ to 16.67 mΩ and 2 V maximum threshold, met by a DMT6007LFG.

VCAP needs at least 0.1 µF and should be ten times the MOSFET input capacitance or more. The input needs at least 22 nF and the output at least 100 nF. A ceramic input bypass above 22 nF is called for when the supply is more than a few inches away.

The TVS breakdown must sit above the worst steady voltages: above the 24 V jump start and the 35 V suppressed load dump on the positive side yet below 65 V, and beyond the -16 V reverse battery on the negative side. ISO 7637-2 pulse 1 drives the input to -150 V through 10 Ω, about 15 A into the TVS. The negative clamp plus the output capacitor voltage must stay within the MOSFET VDS and the -75 V CATHODE to ANODE rating, which limits the clamp to 44 V. An SMBJ33CA (36.7 V breakdown, 600 W peak pulse, clamping at -44 V with 15 A) meets this and covers suppressed load dump (ISO 16750-2 pulse B).

TVS+ breakdown must exceed the 48 V jump start, stay below the 65 V rating of ANODE and EN, and withstand a 65 V suppressed load dump. TVS- must stand off the -32 V reverse battery. Pulse 1 reaches -600 V through 50 Ω, about 12 A, and the clamp is limited to 43 V. One bidirectional part cannot meet a breakdown of at least 65 V with a clamp of at most 43 V, so two unidirectional parts are used back to back: SMBJ58A (64.4 V minimum, 67.8 V typical breakdown) and SMBJ26A (about 32 V breakdown, 42.1 V maximum clamp), with a 75 V MOSFET.

In an OR-ing arrangement each supply has its own controller and MOSFET, ANODE at the supply and CATHODE at the shared load. A reverse drop below -11 mV pulls the gate down within 0.45 µs typical; a forward drop above 50 mV turns the gate back on with 11 mA of gate current. A failing supply is cut off quickly so the output stays up and the other supply is protected.
To protect the controller and its parts from a direct short on the output, the supply feeding it must have overload and short-circuit protection.

Place ANODE, GATE and CATHODE close to the MOSFET source, gate and drain. Use wide copper on the MOSFET source and drain, which carry the load current. Keep the VCAP capacitor away from the MOSFET so heat does not shift its value. Run GATE to the MOSFET gate on a short, not too thin trace; trace resistance there lengthens turn-off delay.

AEC-Q100 qualified: temperature grade 1 (-40 °C to 125 °C ambient), HBM ESD class 2, CDM ESD class C4B. Functional safety capable, with documentation for system design. Meets ISO 7637 automotive transients with a suitable TVS.
